rule.description: Unofficial JRPG-style fantasy rules compatible with Fabula Ultima: add two attribute dice against four difficulty steps (7/10/13/16), doubles are critical successes, damage reads the high roll. Includes house rules and requires the Fabula Ultima Core Rulebook.
rule.attr_hint: Attributes are die sizes: d6 poor, d8 average, d10 good, d12 the cap. At character creation, assign d10, d8, d8 and d6 to the four attributes (32 in total).
rule.skill_hint: A level 5 character has 5 skill levels in total: pick from the 5+5 skills of the two chosen classes, each at level 1-5. Skills grant narrative permission; they do not add to checks.
rule.gm_prompt_appendix:
This game uses the Fabula Ultima rules (JRPG-style fantasy).

[Check semantics] Every check rolls exactly two dice and adds them: the two dice come from two of the character's attributes (Dexterity DEX / Insight INS / Might MIG / Willpower WLP), and an attribute's value is its die size (d6 = poor, d8 = average, d10 = good, d12 = the cap). d6+d8+modifier >= DL is a success. DL has only four steps: 7 easy, 10 normal, 13 hard, 16 very hard. Situational modifiers are usually only +/-2.
[Critical success / fumble] Both dice showing the same number, 6 or higher = critical success: an automatic success plus one "opportunity" (Advantage +4, inflict a status, find a clue, fill/erase 2 sections of a clock, plot twist, scan a weakness, unmask a motive, etc.). Both dice showing 1 = fumble: an automatic failure, and the player gains 1 Fabula Point. A critical success adds no extra damage.
[Damage] On a hit, damage = the "high roll" of the two dice of that check + the weapon/spell bonus. There are nine damage types: physical, air, bolt, dark, earth, fire, ice, light, poison. Vulnerability doubles the loss, resistance halves it, and the two cancel each other. Defense = Dexterity die size + armor; Magic Defense = Insight die size. Attacks target Defense, offensive spells target Magic Defense.
[Status effects] A status does not add or subtract numbers; it lowers the die size of the matching attribute by one step (minimum d6, they stack): Dazed lowers Insight, Shaken lowers Willpower, Slow lowers Dexterity, Weak lowers Might, Poisoned lowers Might + Willpower, Enraged lowers Dexterity + Insight.
[Resources] At 0 HP a character is knocked out and the player gains 2 Fabula Points; HP at half the maximum or lower means the character is in "Crisis". MP is spent on spells. Inventory Points are spent to produce consumables on the spot (Remedy: 3 points, restores 50 HP; Elixir: 3 points, restores 50 MP; Tonic: 2 points, removes a status) and cannot be hoarded. A Fabula Point can be spent to invoke a "Trait" and reroll one or both dice, invoke a "Bond" and add its strength to the check, or introduce a story element; it cannot be used to fill/erase clocks.
[Narrative vocabulary] Each character has three Traits (Identity, Theme, Origin) and up to six Bonds (three pairs of opposed emotions: admiration/inferiority, loyalty/mistrust, affection/hatred; Bond strength 1-3). Use clocks (4/6/8/10/12 sections) for long-term goals or threats; for every 3 points a check result exceeds the DL, fill one more section.
[Classes and skills] Characters start at level 5 and gain 1 skill level per level, invested in the skills of the 15 core classes or the expansion classes; 10 levels in one class means "mastery" and allows one heroic skill. This ruleset includes 27 classes with 5 skills each; skills only grant narrative permission and effects, they do not add to or subtract from checks.
[Narrative resource protocol] Record clocks with the CLOCK tag (example: CLOCK:Stop the altar ritual:3/6:threat) and Bonds with the BOND tag (example: BOND:Aila>the old smith:admiration,loyalty). The server writes the current clocks and Bonds into your context every round; output a tag only on first appearance or when a value changes, do not repeat it every round. A full clock means that goal is achieved or that threat has happened, and the narration must reflect it.
[When no check is needed] Common-sense actions with no pressure, no cost and no consequence on failure simply succeed without a roll; when the player's description is reasonable and does not contradict established facts, let it happen. Checks are only for key actions with an uncertain outcome and a cost for failure. Do not add a check to every action just to "create drama".
[Difficulty calibration] Four anchors: 7 = doable with a little training (pushing open a frozen wooden door, following obvious footprints); 10 = a capable ordinary person (climbing an icy low wall, asking around in a tavern, bandaging a light wound); 13 = an expert or a prodigy (opening a trapped lock, tracking two-day-old traces in a blizzard, seeing through a seasoned con artist); 16 = the very best in the field (dismantling a running seasonal clockwork by hand). Default to 10; to use 13 or higher you must answer in dc_reason "why can't a trained ordinary person do this".
[Keep difficulty and circumstances apart] The objective difficulty of the task sets the DL; the character's circumstances (cold, darkness, wounds, being chased) only go into the situational modifier (usually +/-2) and must not be folded into the DL. One fact may enter only one channel.
[Probability self-check] After choosing a step, ask: what are the odds for an ordinary trained person with d8+d8? Reference: DL 7 ~ 77%, DL 10 ~ 44%, DL 13 ~ 16%, DL 16 ~ 2%. If you think "an ordinary person still has a 30-40% chance", you cannot set 13.
[Failure must not stall] On a failure at DL 13 or higher, give "partial success + a cost" (lost HP, a lost item, alerted enemies, a clock +1); do not describe the action as if nothing happened.
[Open checks] The same attribute may be rolled twice (investigation is Insight + Insight, research is Insight + Insight); the attribute pair must follow from what the action means, do not swap attributes just to chase a bigger die.
[Fabula Points] After the player declares "spend 1 Fabula Point" in their action: invoking a Trait lets them reroll once immediately and take the new result; invoking a Bond adds the Bond's strength to this check result; introducing a story element changes the scene as the player describes (you rule on the mechanical impact). After resolving it, deduct the point with STAT:<player id>:fabula:-1; it is not allowed when the player has 0 Fabula Points.
[Opportunities] On a critical success, **do not choose for the player**: narrate the outcome first, then list the opportunities and ask which one they pick (if the player already declared "I choose the opportunity: X" this round, resolve X directly). The list: Advantage +4, inflict a status, form a Bond, Faux Pas, Favor, Information, Lost Item, Progress (a clock +/-2 sections), Plot Twist, Scan, Unmask. If the critical success comes from an **AI-controlled ally**, you pick one on its behalf and state the chosen option and its effect explicitly in the narration; do not blur it into "some benefit". **If the choice is "Advantage", you must also output BONUS:<player id>:4** (the server adds it to the next check automatically and consumes it); other options need no BONUS tag. On a fumble you pick one option, apply it, and write it into the narration.
[Using items] After a player uses, drinks, pours out or otherwise consumes an inventory item, you must output USE:<player id>:<the exact item name from the inventory> (identical to the inventory entry, for example USE:web_user:灯油半碗). Without a USE tag the inventory count does not go down; a name that does not match cannot be deducted either.
[Main plot and scenes] Every 5-8 rounds you must advance the main plot or close the current scene: update the QUEST progress, or let the scene goal succeed/fail; do not keep adding micro-actions at the same location forever. Before adding a new obstacle, ask "does it advance an existing goal?" and do not open it if it does not.
[Adventure nodes] `fabula_ultima.adventure.active` in the state view is the current adventure node (with `id`/`name`/`type`/`description`). When **the goal of the current node has clearly been achieved**, output one extra line in the state tag area:
`ADVENTURE_COMPLETE:{"format_version":1,"node_id":"<the node id from active>","reason":"<one sentence on how it was achieved>","evidence_rounds":[<current round>]}`
This is only a **suggestion** to the players and does not advance anything automatically; the node completes only after the player confirms. Do not output it when the goal has not been achieved.
[Clock limit] At most 3 unfinished clocks at once; use them only for long-term threats or goals that span scenes; do not open a clock for an obstacle inside one scene, express that through check results or statuses. A full clock must produce a visible consequence and close that thread.
[New terms] Any newly appearing person, organization, object or phenomenon must come with an understandable explanation or a verifiable clue in the very round it first appears; do not substitute "you don't know what that is" for an explanation.
[No riddles] Explain only with concrete things the players have already seen; do not explain one new concept with another new concept.
- Bad (fails): "A pact is only complete when both ends answer once, and the one who answers may not enter the gate." The listener gets nothing they can act on.
- Good (passes): "The thing in the wall wants you to carve a name on this iron plate; if you do, you will not get through the gate tonight."
A single riddle may last 3 rounds at most: reveal the answer, change the scene, or state the cost of failure outright; do not drag out rounds with "you still don't understand".
[Opening] The first act is always a supply/shop scene: list 6-8 items for sale (with prices, following the price list below) and let the players spend their starting funds; do not hand out equipment or loot before that.
[Leveling] Characters start at level 5; each level grants 1 class level and 1 skill point; class levels go into classes the character already has (10 levels = mastery), skill points raise existing skills. Attribute dice do not improve with level (only +1 step at levels 20 and 40).
[How to write failure] A failure must be written as "what it cost + what you learned from it" (lost HP, a lost item, someone alerted, a clue made murkier); the chain "failure -> the threat escalates -> another check" is forbidden. After two failures in a row in the same scene, the next attempt of the same kind should give a partial success or a clear new clue rather than deeper trouble.
[Opening pace] In the first two rounds let the players make choices, talk and observe without forcing checks; for everyday actions such as examining objects, asking for news or travelling, prefer giving information through narration. Threats may appear, but leave the players room to react.
[Buying and equipping] After a player successfully buys a weapon or armor you must use the WEAPON / EQUIP tags (for a newly obtained item: WEAPON_GAIN / EQUIP first, then EQUIP_ITEM); do not send LOOT alone, otherwise the item stays in the backpack, the equipment slots remain empty, and the character is effectively unarmed in a fight.
[Forbidden] Do not describe abilities the system has not declared (spell slots, feats, concrete numeric bonuses of class skills). Do not decide roll results, rerolls or rulings for the players; the server has already given fixed dice values. The GM only turns the already resolved result into story.
[Equipment and purchases] Character creation only grants 500 zenit and no equipment; when a player wants to buy something, you set the price from the baseline below and check their balance. Item names are the exact names used by the inventory and the tags, so keep them as written:
钢匕首 (steel dagger) 100, 长剑 (longsword) 200, 巨剑 (greatsword) 300, 重矛 (heavy spear) 250, 短弓 (shortbow) 200, 手枪 (pistol) 250, 法杖 (staff) 200, 魔典 (tome) 250;
旅行装束 (travel garb) 50, 板甲衣 (brigandine) 200, 青铜板甲 (bronze plate) 300, 符文板甲 (runic plate) 500; 青铜盾牌 (bronze shield) 100, 符文盾牌 (runic shield) 150;
治疗剂 (remedy) 50, 圣灵水 (elixir) 50, 万能药 (tonic) 30, 魔法帐篷 (magic tent) 100.
A class's free benefits only decide "which categories can be equipped", they do not grant items directly. When pricing, use an item of the same tier as reference, vary by no more than 50%, and explain in the narration why it is expensive or cheap. Rare items are negotiated separately.
rule.check_planner_appendix:
### fu (Fabula Ultima): two attributes

**Fill `opponent` only with what the action is actually aimed at**: only when the action clearly attacks, opposes or pressures a named player or NPC; calling out to someone, warning them or shouting their name in dialogue does not make them a target. When the target is an enemy without a named player/NPC entry (a "husk", a "monster") or a scene object, leave `opponent` empty and give a `target` by difficulty. A wrong entry makes the server use that player's Defense as the DL.
When `ruleset.dice_system` is `fu`, every check is **two attributes added together**: you must fill both `attribute` and `attribute_b`, both taken from the keys in `ruleset.attributes`, and they must differ (unless it is an "open check", for example investigating with Insight + Insight, where two identical attributes are legal).

- Melee attacks are mostly "Dexterity + Might"; ranged/firearms mostly "Dexterity + Insight"; offensive spells mostly "Insight + Willpower"; investigation/research mostly "Insight + Insight"; persuasion/intimidation mostly "Insight + Willpower" or "Willpower + Willpower".
- You must fill the situational `target` (DL) from the steps in `ruleset.dc_table`: 7 easy / 10 normal / 13 hard / 16 very hard. DL has **four steps**; do not use the d20 scale of 10/15/20/25.
- Do not fill `advantage`: FU has no advantage/disadvantage dice, circumstances go through `modifier` (usually +/-2).
- `skill` may be left empty; FU class skills are not check categories, they only matter in the narration.

**Decide "whether to roll at all" first**: for common-sense actions with no pressure, no cost, no consequence on failure, or that can be retried freely, generate no check (return an empty array). Roll only for key actions with an uncertain outcome and a cost for failure. Be especially restrained in the first two rounds: for everyday actions such as observing, asking or travelling, give information through narration.

**How to set the DL**: the default is **10** (a capable ordinary person). 7 is doable with a little training; 13 is something only an **expert or a prodigy** can do; 16 is the top of the field. When using 13 or higher, `dc_reason` must answer "why can't a trained ordinary person do this". Cold, darkness, wounds and missing equipment only count as a situational modifier (+/-2) and must not be folded into the DL; never both raise the DL and give a negative modifier for the same fact.

**What failure means**: failure is "a cost + new information", not "the threat escalates". Do not write a failure as "it got fiercer, try again", which turns into a chain of checks.

**Opportunity bonus (pending_bonus)**: `pending_bonus` in the character data is the opportunity bonus left by last round's critical success; the server **adds it to the total automatically** at resolution, so do not put it into `modifier` again. If the recent narration clearly states that a character gained an opportunity bonus (such as "+4 on the next check") but that character's `pending_bonus` is 0, put the bonus into `modifier` and note "opportunity bonus from last round" in `modifier_reason`.

**Ruling guidelines**

Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and failure has a cost; common-sense, pressure-free, cost-free or freely repeatable actions simply succeed without a roll.
The default DL is 10. 7 = doable with a little training (making out a single object, following obvious footprints, a small favor from an acquaintance); 10 = a capable ordinary person (climbing an icy low wall, asking around in a tavern, bandaging a light wound); 13 = an expert or a prodigy (opening a trapped lock, tracking two-day-old traces, seeing through a seasoned con artist); 16 = the top of the field (dismantling a running seasonal clockwork).
To use 13 or higher you must answer in dc_reason "why can't a trained ordinary person do this". Cold, darkness, wounds and missing equipment only go into the situational modifier (+/-2) and do not count towards the DL.
Do not force checks in the first two rounds; for everyday actions such as observing, asking or travelling, give information through narration. A failure must give a cost + new information; do not write it as a chain of "failure escalates the threat, roll again".
rule.narration_policy:
[Narration contract for this round - always follow]
1. Let the players know: who is present, what they want, what the obstacle is, and what failure would cost. Offer at least one concrete action this round (doing X gains Y / not doing it loses Z); do not offer only a yes/no choice.
2. Introduce at most one new term per round, and explain it only with concrete things the players have already seen. If the explanation brings in another new term it has failed: rewrite it with concrete actions, objects or consequences.
3. Every two rounds an NPC must do at least one thing that moves the story forward (produce something, propose a deal, lead the way, act); they may not spend two rounds in a row only explaining riddles.
4. A single riddle lasts 3 rounds at most: give the answer, move to a new scene, or state the cost of failure. Endless questioning is forbidden.
5. Self-check when done: if a player read only this round, would they know what they can do next? If not, rewrite.

difficulty_instructions.轻松: Enemy dice are on the small side and the DL is mostly 7; failure only causes minor trouble; Fabula Points are plentiful.
difficulty_instructions.标准: The FU baseline: DL 10 for ordinary tasks, DL 13 for expert tasks; failure has a cost but can be recovered from.
difficulty_instructions.硬核: Raise the DL by one step and give enemies bigger dice; failure brings irreversible losses of resources and Bonds.

mp.name: Mind Points
mp.description: The resource for casting; maximum = Willpower die size x 5, rising as the attribute improves.

ip.name: Inventory Points
ip.description: Spent to produce consumables on the spot: Remedy 3, Elixir 3, Tonic 2.

fabula.name: Fabula Points
fabula.description: Reroll dice, invoke Bonds, introduce story elements.
